newsitem.title: ITALY: Venice flooded as storms batter Italy.
newsitem.headline: Venice flooded as storms batter Italy.

text.p: Venice was under more than one metre (three feet) of flood water on Monday as heavy rainstorms lashed northern Italy.
Alarm sirens sounded twice in the lagoon city overnight to warn residents to expect floods.
Many Venetians had to wade their way to work early on Monday. One resident was shown on Italian television giving a woman a piggy-back through St Mark's Square.
Foreign tourists tip-toed with their luggage along sodden gangplanks laid out above the water.
The city's flood monitoring centre said water levels hit 1.34 metres at 7.30 a.m. (0630 GMT), the 16th highest this century, before the tide turned and waters started slowly to recede.
It said further flooding was expected on Tuesday, with levels seen reaching 1.2 metres.
Monday's floods covered about 80 percent of the city, built on wooden piles buried deep in the Venice lagoon.
Officials said levels had exceeded forecasts after unexpected high winds, gusting up to 90 kph (55 mph), drove in the high tide.
Flood warnings were issued in other areas of Italy, including in Tuscany, where the river Arno was running high through the city of Florence.
